Articles

Guides

From references to networks

What a projected network is, how a table of citations becomes a bibliographic coupling network, which similarity measure and threshold to choose, and how to cut a corpus into time windows.

Finding and reading clusters

What community detection does, how the Leiden algorithm and its resolution shape the clusters, how to check their stability, and how to name and characterise them.

Drawing networks

How a layout turns a network into a map: force-directed layouts (Fruchterman-Reingold, Kamada-Kawai, ForceAtlas2), UMAP, and how to colour, label and draw the clusters.

Following clusters over time

How to detect clusters in each time window, link them across windows into dynamic clusters, and draw their history as an alluvial plot.

Beyond bibliographic coupling

The same pipeline for co-citation, for authors instead of articles, and for any two-mode table; and why the identifiers of references matter.
